title: The Delegation Dilemma: Economies of Scale, Accountability, and Polycentric Governance
abstract: arXiv:2610.21746v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Many collective-action systems are neither fully decentralized nor fully centralized: agents voluntarily organize into institutions that share organizational costs and delegate decisions to representatives. Delegation can reduce individual costs, but it also transfers control to representatives whose private objectives need not align with those of their constituents. We study this tension in a repeated game with endogenous delegation to self-interested centers. A simple reduced-form model yields a scale--accountability tradeoff: larger constituencies offer greater cost-sharing benefits to members, yet the marginal value to a center of retaining any one constituent decreases as group size grows. Consequently, the prospect of individual exit can sustain non-exploitative delegation only up to an endogenous accountable constituency size. translated_title: 委托困境：规模经济、问责制与多中心治理
translated_abstract: 许多集体行动系统既不是完全去中心化的，也不是完全中心化的：参与者自愿组织成共享组织成本、并将决策委托给代表机构的制度。委托可以降低个体成本，但也会将控制权转移给代表，而代表的私人目标未必与其委托人一致。我们在一个存在内生委托给自利中心的重复博弈中研究这种张力。一个简单的简化形式模型得出了规模—问责权衡：更大的委托群体为成员提供更大的成本分担收益，但对中心而言，保留任何单个成员的边际价值随着群体规模的增大而下降。因此，个体退出的可能性只能在某个内生的问责群体规模上限之内维持非剥削性的委托关系。此外，我们还识别出在可行条件下能够实现完全委托的问责治理的参数区域。
tldr: 该论文通过重复博弈模型揭示了委托治理中的“规模—问责”权衡：更大的群体虽带来更多成本分担收益，却削弱了中心保留单个成员的激励，从而内生地决定了可持续的非剥削性委托的群体规模上限。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals a scale-accountability tradeoff in delegated governance via a repeated game model: larger constituencies yield greater cost-sharing benefits but reduce the center's marginal incentive to retain any individual member, thereby endogenously bounding the accountable constituency size for non-exploitative delegation.
